links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses about hidradenitis suppurativa (FRES, FKGL) versus recommended patient reading level
links.effect: All three chatbots produced text at college or postgraduate reading level; none achieved the necessary readability level. Copilot had better readability scores (P < .001).
links.quote: All the AI models had difficult reading levels as college or postgraduate.

links.outcome: Reading grade level of chatbot patient information (FKGL, FRES) relative to appropriate level
links.effect: None of the chatbots achieved the necessary readability level; Perplexity had higher FKGL (P = .001) and lower FRES (P = .001) in the test/procedure & drug category; outputs at college or postgraduate level.
links.quote: Nevertheless, none of the chatbots achieved the necessary level of readability.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of three LLM chatbots (ChatGPT-4o, Copilot, Perplexity) answering consumer search queries regarding hidradenitis suppurativa, assessing quality, readability, and accuracy without evaluating a specific implementation safeguard.
